reasons: The excerpt states that Clarity was completely free with no data limit at the time of recording, while Hotjar had traffic-based pricing that became costly at higher volume.
It explicitly says the presenter was moving many clients from Hotjar to Clarity for that reason because the platforms “pretty much do the same thing” for heatmaps and recordings.
The all-in-one preference is a stated reason to favor Hotjar, so it is a supported exclusion from this Clarity-focused recommendation.
The excerpt directly characterizes Hotjar as doing pretty much the same thing as Clarity for user recordings, scroll/click heatmap information, and related core behavior-analysis functions.

The source describes Clarity area maps as showing the percentage of clicks going to different website areas and explicitly gives navigation clicks and diverted attention as examples of what to inspect.
The candidate appropriately does not invent a numerical threshold or decision rule for the click percentages.
The source says Hotjar engagement zones can be found from the heatmap map types and show sections with higher engagement.

It expressly frames Clarity area maps as easier for the presenter to interpret and use for insight; the candidate preserves this as an interpretive judgment rather than an objective performance result.
The excerpt states that Hotjar has website surveys whereas Clarity does not.
It specifically proposes exit-intent questions about what stopped a purchase, almost stopped a conversion, or prompted the visitor to leave.
The separately paid-survey dependency is supported by the source’s statement that surveys and feedback cost extra beyond the heatmap and recording software.
The source says the presenter often uses post-purchase surveys immediately after purchase for clients.
The proposed questions about purchase motivation and near-abandonment are directly given in the excerpt.
The source also supports the linked additional-cost condition for Hotjar survey functionality.
The recommendation to use Okendo, install it, and collect unlimited responses subject to order data is stated in the excerpt.

However, the candidate turns “This is particularly for Shopify stores” into an absolute prerequisite that the store be Shopify. The excerpt identifies Shopify as a particular use case, not an exclusive eligibility requirement.
The Hotjar-survey-fee concern is a supported reason to consider an alternative, but it is not stated as a required trigger for all Okendo use.
The excerpt supports that the presenter often uses UserBrain instead of Hotjar and describes remote testing prompts for first impressions, cart/checkout, and a B2B form-finding task.

The candidate changes the source’s “finding the contract form” wording to “finding the contact form.” The supplied excerpt does not say “contact form,” so that correction cannot be certified from this source alone.
Its unqualified title, “instead of Hotjar,” overstates the source’s narrower statement that the presenter often ends up using UserBrain instead.
The source says Hotjar offers user interviews, identifies the feature as newer, and explicitly leaves whether the added cost is worthwhile as arguable.
The candidate correctly preserves this as unresolved rather than claiming that Hotjar interviews are or are not worth the cost.

The excerpt says Hotjar can create custom navigation funnels and says that the same thing can be set up from the GA4 Explore tab, including the stated B2B homepage-to-contact-form-to-thank-you-page example.

However, the candidate’s exclusion is backwards: “GA4 already has this functionality built in” is presented by the source as the reason to use GA4 for the funnel, not as a condition excluding the action.
The final consensus in the excerpt says Hotjar is the best bet for someone seeking heatmaps, recordings, user interviews, surveys, and funnels in one tool.
The candidate retains the important qualification that many of those features still require separate payment.
The source explicitly recommends Microsoft Clarity as the best bet for the core use case of heatmap data and user-recording data.
Its time-qualified limitation is appropriate because the free/no-data-limit basis was stated only as of the recording.
The core conditional recommendation is supported: if someone is comfortable using separate tools such as Okendo and UserBrain, the presenter says there is no real downside and favors Clarity.

The hard depends_on relations overstate the excerpt. The source says separate tools “like” Okendo and UserBrain may be used; it does not say that choosing Clarity requires both tools, nor that it requires Okendo specifically, which the excerpt describes as particularly for Shopify stores.
The main pricing claim is supported: the source states a $32/month Plus plan with 100 daily sessions and says costs tend to rise substantially at higher numbers.

However, the candidate’s unknown claiming that the exact tier name is unclear is contradicted by the excerpt, which explicitly calls it the “Plus plan.” Variations in the transcript’s rendering of Hotjar do not make that plan name unclear.
The source explicitly says Hotjar surveys and feedback require additional payment beyond the heatmap and recording software.
It also says this separate survey component can add substantially to fees, while not specifying the amount.

omissions.description: Use heatmaps to assess scroll depth or the proportion of visitors who reach a particular part of a page, not only click behavior.
omissions.quote: you can look at heat map data so how far are people scrolling where are they clicking

omissions.description: Use an area-map finding to prioritize an A/B test: when a highly clicked lower-page section is reached by relatively few visitors, move its icons higher on the homepage; the source reports one such test and outcome.
omissions.quote: on this on our client site we saw that 10.41% of clicks were going towards the shop by industry section that was kind of further down the page but you know only 30 to 35% of people were actually reaching this section so it was one of the highest clicked elements on the page but very few people were reaching there and so we ran a simple AB test where we actually put those same icons at the top of the homepage to kind of send people into the collection pages and get further down the funnel um and so with that AB test we saw an 18% uh in conversions just from that one um AB test alone

source_limitations: The excerpt is an informal spoken transcript with apparent transcription inconsistencies in product names and at least one unclear price-related trailing token (“4 Z”).
Pricing, free-tier, and no-data-limit statements are explicitly limited to “the time of this recording,” but the recording date is not supplied.
The comparative recommendations and ease-of-interpretation assessment are primarily the presenter’s views and client experience, not a documented independent evaluation.
The reported 18% conversion result is a single example; the excerpt provides no sample size, test duration, baseline, statistical method, or other validation details.
The excerpt does not provide platform documentation or detailed feature, data-retention, sampling, integration, or privacy comparisons.
